items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I had not heard too many trumpet players except Dolly and Dyer Jones, Sydney de Paris, John Nesbit, Freddie Jenkins and the fellow from New Orleans that played around town on a wagon.

ctx.x: It was at Carpenter's house that I heard my first Victor record. It was by a trumpet-player named Johnny Dunn and the side I remember was a blues called "I've Been Down So Long". The second line was: "Until down don't worry me".

I can not describe Johnny Dunn's style, but I had not heard anyone play the way he did. In fact I had not heard too many trumpet players except Dolly and Dyer Jones, Sydney de Paris, John Nesbit, Freddie Jenkins and the fellow from New Orleans that played around town on a wagon. There were mostly cornet players in the marching bands but they never played jazz and I listened to these bands and heard all the musicians as anyone else who loved music.

I did not care too much about the way Johnny Dunn played, but I did copy the way he played "I've Been Down So Long", because I was learning the trumpet and it was something to help me learn the horn better.
